result.answer_preview:
Based on the provided evidence, it is impossible to quote a passage where Parmenides uses the phrase *liberum arbitrium* [1].
Parmenides was a pre-Socratic Greek philosopher, whereas *liberum arbitrium* is a Latin term [1], [2]. The terminology surrounding the concept of free will evolved from Greek to Latin over time, and it was these later Latin neologisms that shaped subsequent Western philosophical discussions [2]. Because of this linguistic and chronological barrier, a pre-Socratic Greek philosopher could not have used this Latin vocabulary [2].
Furthermore, the historical record indicates that the phrase did not exist during Parmenides' lifetime; rather, "[t]he earliest attestation of the compound phrase is in Tertullian, Adversus Marcionem II.6.3," which dates to a much later period in antiquity [1]. Therefore, no such quotation from Parmenides exists [1], [2].
